caption: What if one grain of rice doubled on every square of a chessboard? Chess grew out of chaturanga, first known from India, and an old legend says its inventor asked the king for rice: 1 grain on the first square, 2 on the second, 4 on the third, doubling every time. At about 20 mg a grain, square 11 holds 1,024 grains, about a spoonful. Square 21: over 1 million grains, roughly a 20 kg sack. Square 31: over 1 billion, about 20 tonnes. Square 41: over 1 trillion, a cargo ship's load. Square 55 alone would be more than double India's record yearly harvest of about 150 million tonnes. All 64 squares: 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 grains, more than 500 years of the world's entire rice crop. The twist: the last square alone holds 1 grain more than all 63 before it combined. Would YOU have taken the deal? 👇
